outcomes.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, envisions itself to become a catalyst for the wholistic transformational development of Catholic Augustinian Marian graduates rooted in Gospel values.

mission.lead: To achieve the above vision, LCUP commits itself to generate and make available to its Augustinian Marian students, programs and services that will make them:
items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
develop individuals who are resilient, inclusive and responsive to be socio-economic realities of the Philippines and the complexities of the global environment.

pos.text: Ability to apply knowledge of mathematics and science to solve complex engineering problems;
Ability to design and conduct experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret data;

Ability to design a system, component, or process to meet desired needs within realistic constraints such as economic, environmental, social, political, ethical, health and safety, manufacturability and sustainability, in accordance with standards.

Recognition of the need for, and an ability to engage in life-long learning;

Ability to design, develop, implement and improve integrated system that include people materials, implementation, equipment and energy.

description.t:
This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

clos.title: CLO 1
clos.statement: Identify the design process of electronic circuits and systems and conduct experiments involving sensors and mixed-signal systems, analyze data, and interpret results to improve performance and reliability.

clos.title: CLO 2
clos.statement: Develop analytical and design skills for both analog and digital electronic circuit and implement sensor-based systems that integrate hardware and software components while considering economic, environmental, and ethical constraints.

clos.title: CLO 3
clos.statement: Analyze and apply the behavior of passive components in AC circuits and their instrumentation applications in multidisciplinary teams to design, test, and optimize mixed-signal and sensor applications for engineering solutions

clos.title: CLO 4
clos.statement: Exhibit lifelong learning, precision, and ethical responsibility in performing measurements and calibration tasks. Engage in continuous learning by exploring emerging technologies and trends in sensors, instrumentation, and mixed-signal design for future innovation
